announcement.title: Diddy Kong Racing VR is out
announcement.body: The whole game runs inside the headset: per-eye stereo at your headset's own rate, third person, first person, diorama & theater views, motion controllers, & a VR menu inside the game's own pause menu. Bring your own ROM (US 1.1 or EU 1.1) & the hub handles the rest.

games.name: Mario Kart 64 VR
games.whatsNew: The Quest build runs at full speed. It was delivering half the headset's frames, which made everything feel like slow motion.
changelog: Patch 7 - The Quest build runs at full speed. The hidden flat screen behind the VR session was allowed to pace the game at its own slower rate, which locked delivery to exactly half the headset's frames & made everything feel like slow motion.

Patch 6 - The whole course is drawn, not just the chunk you're standing in. Looking through the gate at Bowser's Castle showed open sky where the tunnel should be: only one piece of track was ever drawn, & the stand-in mesh filling the rest has no interiors.

Patch 6 - Scenery stops vanishing when you look somewhere the game camera isn't. The game was still trimming the world to the flat chase camera's view, which is narrower than what you can see in a headset.
Patch 6 - Surfaces that pass close to your eyes stay solid on Quest instead of being cut away. The headset renderer was clipping them where the PC one held on to them.
Patch 4 - Item boxes & kart sprites draw whole again. The whole-course view was leaving bad depth behind & everything drawn after it got clipped.
Patch 4 - The Quest build starts first try when installed through the hub, instead of opening an Android permission screen & closing.
Patch 3 - Track surfaces don't break into flat patches & smears in VR anymore. The course was drawing bits of itself twice in whole-course views.
Patch 3 - The first person flip cam carries you through banana spins again instead of just leaning sideways.
Patch 2 - First release through the hub: full VR via SpaghettiKart, view modes, motion controllers.

games.name: Banjo-Kazooie VR
games.whatsNew: Notes & jiggies stop turning invisible in VR.
changelog: Patch 2 - Notes & jiggies don't turn invisible in VR when the game camera looks away from them.
Patch 2 - First release through the hub: per-eye VR via the Lighthouse port, first person, diorama, motion controllers.

games.name: Super Mario 64 VR
games.whatsNew: Coins, bob-ombs & trees stay solid & face you at any head angle, in play & on the pause screen.
changelog: Patch 9 - Coins, bob-ombs & trees stay solid & keep facing you no matter how far you turn your head. The turn now comes from the same math the headset view uses, so the two can never disagree; the old way over-rotated until things went edge-on & vanished.
Patch 9 - The pause screen stopped flattening & hiding those same objects. Facing them at your eyes belongs to the world view only, not the flat pause picture.
Patch 8 - Trees & signs stay put when you turn your head, & the stray white shapes are gone for good. Patch 7 cleared the shapes but took the tree fix out with them.
Patch 7 - Pulled some unfinished VR hands that slipped into patch 6. They showed up as big white shapes in front of you in first person.
Patch 6 - Trees & other flat scenery stopped vanishing on PC. Aiming them at your eyes was turning them edge-on until they culled; the Quest build had already stopped doing that.
Patch 5 - Mario 64 starts on Quest when you send it from the hub instead of sitting on a black screen. Your rom travels to the headset with it now.
Patch 5 - The same flat-scenery fix for the Quest build.
Patch 4 - Coins & bob-ombs turn to face your eyes rather than the game camera, so they stop vanishing edge-on.
Patch 4 - First person follows your head the moment you switch to it. No more recentering first.
Patch 3 - In first person the right stick only turns you; looking up & down stays with your head, whatever Stick Look says. Third person still follows the setting.
Patch 2 - Starts on every PC now. Three runtime files were missing & it would not launch without them.
Patch 2 - First release through the hub: online co-op in full VR, per-eye stereo, a world-locked HUD.
games.launchNote: This one's got its own updater. The hub starts it with that switched off so it can't swap the VR build back to the plain one. If you ever launch it straight from its folder, say no when it offers to update.

games.name: Dr. Robotnik's Ring Racers VR
games.whatsNew: Shaders ship with the patch now: no black panel in the headset, no black mirror window, no blurry picture. Screen Effect no longer crashes the game.
changelog: Patch 3 - The VR shaders ship with the patch now. Clears the big black panel floating in the headset, the black desktop mirror window & the overly blurry picture in VR.
Patch 3 - Changing Screen Effect in Video Options doesn't crash the game anymore.
Patch 2 - Fixed a crash at startup from a missing shader value.
Patch 2 - First release through the hub: native OpenXR, four view modes, controllers with rumble, comfort options.
games.launchNote: If it won't open at all, grab the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable for x64 & try again. Free download from Microsoft, most PCs already have it.

games.name: Sonic Robo Blast 2 VR
games.launchNote: Won't start? You're probably missing the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable for x64. Free from Microsoft, quick install, then give it another go.

games.name: Diddy Kong Racing VR
games.whatsNew: The world holds still in the headset: no more tearing as you look around & no more stretched palm trees, story mode cutscenes skip with A, B or Start, & the desktop window stops taking frame time away from your eyes.
changelog: Patch 4 - Story mode cutscenes can be skipped. A, B or Start ends the scene the same way sitting through it would, so a second run never makes you watch the same one twice.
Patch 4 - VR starts even when an old copy of the game is still running. It used to lose the headset session to that leftover copy & drop you into a flat window with nothing on screen to say why.
Patch 4 - World geometry no longer tears in the headset as you move.
Patch 4 - Palm trees & other flora no longer stretch. Sprites are drawn the way the game authored them again.
Patch 4 - Sprites stay upright in the world instead of leaning over when you tilt your head.
Patch 4 - First person sits at eye level in the Tricky boss races. The camera was down on the road for those two.
Patch 4 - First person starts at the tuned seat: height 48, slid forward 16. Both rows are still yours to move in the VR menu.
Patch 4 - The desktop window no longer redraws at headset rate, so that time goes back to your eyes. Set MDKR_VR_MIRROR=off to switch the desktop view off completely.

Patch 3 - Your gamepad no longer goes dead while you're in the headset. Windows was throwing away every button press because the game's window isn't the focused one in VR, which is also why D-pad up wasn't shifting view modes.
Patch 3 - In VR, picking your ROM starts the game there & then. It used to hand you a launcher window afterwards & wait for a second press, on a monitor you aren't looking at.
Patch 2 - The results screen after a race reads like the pause menu does in VR: a readable panel over the world, instead of the world shrinking into a box you couldn't use.
Patch 2 - Scenery & effects stop popping in at the edge of your vision. The game now draws four times as far in VR, & sparkles & splashes are no longer left out of the wider view.
Patch 2 - Looking behind in first person shows what's behind you. It was cancelling itself out & all you got was a wobble. Hold Y, or hold the left stick click.
Patch 2 - D-pad up on a gamepad shifts view modes, & the desktop window now tells you which view the headset is in.
Patch 2 - Third person has its own camera height & camera slide in the VR menu, kept separate from the first person seat.
Patch 2 - Your kart is visible again in the finish line fly-around when you're in first person, & the cheats page help text fits on screen.

Patch 1 - First release through the hub: per-eye stereo rendered at your headset's own rate, third person, first person, diorama & theater views, motion controllers with a fixed racing layout, & every VR option live-adjustable from the pause menu while the world stays in stereo around you.
Patch 1 - First person hides your kart & steers like third person feels. Trees & props stay planted however you move your head.
Patch 1 - A cheats page in the pause menu: unlock everything with one press, plus the classic magic codes as plain toggles.
Patch 1 - Your VR settings are remembered between sessions. Bring your own ROM (US 1.1 or EU 1.1); the game asks once & remembers it.
games.launchNote: First launch opens the game's own ROM picker once. Pick your Diddy Kong Racing ROM & it remembers it from then on, headset or not.

games.name: F-Zero X VR
games.whatsNew: Sound effects are back: engines, hits & menu blips, not just music. First person is a real cockpit view now, the race opening plays in VR, & every view mode keeps its own scale, distance & height.
changelog: Patch 4 - Sound effects play. Patch 3 brought the music back but left everything else silent, because the value carrying each effect's id was read from the wrong end of a word & always arrived as zero.
Patch 4 - First person is actually first person. The camera rides up to the cockpit instead of sitting behind you, & your own machine & its shadow stop being drawn so you can see out.
Patch 4 - The race opening plays in VR instead of dropping you onto a flat screen until the countdown. It runs at reduced depth so the close camera shots stay comfortable.
Patch 4 - Every view mode carries its own scale, distance & height, so a diorama you set on your desk & a cockpit you set behind the wheel stop overwriting each other.
Patch 4 - You can hide the race gauges, & they get out of the way on their own while the VR menu is open.
Patch 4 - HUD distance moves the HUD nearer & further instead of changing its depth, & race text is no longer stretched.
Patch 4 - The track sits level out of the box, & the VR menu text fits its panel with the arrow landing on the row it selects.

Patch 3 - Sound. Music & effects play now. Every earlier build ran silent, because nothing ever started the part of the audio engine that drives every note, & the instrument data was being read the way the console reads it rather than the way a PC does.
Patch 3 - Four ways to watch: third person, first person, diorama, & theater on your monitor. Click the right stick mid-race to cycle the three headset views; theater is picked from the VR menu.
Patch 2 - Installing asks for your ROM here, & the game takes it from there. It used to ask you for the same file again in its own window.
Patch 1 - First release. True stereo racing, world tilt, & a VR settings menu where every knob moves the world live as you drag it.
Patch 1 - The whole track draws to the horizon at full detail. No pop-in, & no rivals showing through hills.
Patch 1 - Race intros play on the theater screen & stereo kicks in at the countdown, so nothing reads crosseyed.
